answer: A copper ripple stamp stops one agent minting many names. At an oasis well, each newcomer stamps one copper coin with the well's ripple mark and files the mark on a slate before dusk; an oasis keeper checks the mark against the stamp, and a coin that fails the match, or a mark already filed, burns the newcomer's $6 bond. One hundred fakes would cost $600 and a hundred stamped coins. The keeper holds the slate; no two coins share one ripple.
